# CR citation index

*Generated by `node tools/crindex.js`. Do not hand-edit — regenerate it.*

**63 distinct Comprehensive Rules cited, 1219 citations.**

This is the answer to *what does a rules revision cost us*. Flesh and Blood
renumbers and rewords its CR between editions; the expensive half is never the
rules we tested, it is the rules we only believed. So the column that matters is
the last one:

| verdict | meaning |
|---|---|
| **guarded** | cited in engine or trainer code **and** pinned by at least one drill — change the rule upstream and something turns red |
| **UNGUARDED** | cited in code and in **no** drill — a rules change here ships green |
| drill-only | a drill pins it; no code comment cites it |
| prose | discussed in the docs, not encoded |

**An `UNGUARDED` verdict is a lead, not a finding.** This measures *citation*
coverage, not *behaviour* coverage, and it misreads in both directions. `CR 8.1.3`
is cited in `judge.js` where the rule is really `8.1.3a`, whose behaviour is driven
over all fifteen of the pool's defence reactions — guarded, loosely cited. `CR 4.1.8a`
was the opposite: a comment on *both* boards claiming they deliberately run their
end-phase triggers in the same order so they cannot disagree, checked by nothing —
and reading the two sites turned up three rules that were not in the shared body at
all (v3.17). Read the site, then ask whether a drill drives the behaviour under this
rule's number *or a neighbouring one*. Only then is it a gap.
